question: The current population of a town is 14,680. It increases by 25% and 70% in two successive years but decreases by 20% in the third year. What is the population of the town at the end of the third year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the percentage changes into multiplying fractions: +25% = 5/4, +70% = 17/10, and −20% = 4/5.

Final Population = Initial Population × (5/4) × (17/10) × (4/5)

Notice that the fraction (5/4) and (4/5) perfectly cancel each other out.

Final Population = 14680 × (17/10) = 1468 × 17 = 24956.

**∴ The correct answer is 24,956.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Population = 14,680

Population change in 1st year = +25%

Population change in 2ⁿd year = +70%

Population change in 3rd year = −20%
